title: Add the ability to initialize the cache (and orchestrate its refreshment)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Hello,

This is a suggestion for adding feature to initialize the cache (and orchestrate its refreshment).

Here's one of my current needs: I have an application with lots of pages. For each page, there are several cached functions that take a few minutes to execute but have a relatively long ttl (several days). The problem is that the user experience is degraded for the first user to access a page.

What would be nice, I think, is to be able to run all pages in the background (without rendering) to initialize the cache, or to be able to run a function or a page in the background (with different query params), and to be able to empty and refill the cache from time to time.

That does sound like a useful feature, thanks for suggesting it [USER]!

I think this could be rephrased as "Implement an app startup hook".

I would imagine something like this, where a startup hook would be passed in at boot:
```
streamlit run --startup_hook my_module.startup.init_app app.py
```
Here, you might have a `my_module/startup.py` file with a `def init_app():` in it to call on boot.

This could then start background threads to do things like populate caches - and the contract could be that the Streamlit wasn't started until the hook exited, allowing the author to block on code execution.

## Update

Streamlit 1.61 will support a `refresh_mode="background"` for `cache_data` and `cache_resource` which allows expired values (based on `ttl`) to be updated in the background without blocking the user session.

It is also already possible to pre-warm caches at startup before the first user connects via `st.App` lifespan:

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from streamlit.starlette import App

[USER]
async def lifespan(app):
    print("🚀 Pre-caching data...")

    # Call cached functions to populate cache
    from myapp import load_data, compute_stats
    load_data("users")      # [USER].cache_data
    load_data("products")   # [USER].cache_data
    compute_stats()         # [USER].cache_resource

    print("✅ Cache warmed!")
    yield
    
    # Run any close operations here

app = App("main.py", lifespan=lifespan)
```

The lifespan runs before the server accepts connections, so the first user gets instant cached results.

We are also planning to add a background job utility (+ cron scheduling) that would allow additional advanced ways to refresh caches in the background. This is tracked here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6687

Thank you so much for this [USER] :) Is there any way that we can influence the "2 * ttl" background cache timeout? In my use case I want a short ttl so the values are updated often, but I never want my users to have to wait for a response. I would like to set the ttl to something like 2 minutes, but the oldest background cache thats allowed to be served can be much older than four minutes. The main goal being that I would prefer old cache over users having to wait.
[USER] i think we can add a config option to make the multiplier configurable. Would this work for you?
